name: Difficulty-to-rung starter
description: Turns the planner's difficulty rating into a starting rung on the deep-worker ladder, normalising synonyms and unknown ratings and respecting an operator mapping, with no additional model call.
advantages: Free at runtime because it reuses a rating the planner already produced.
disadvantages: Quality depends entirely on the planner's rating, and hard work is not started on a stronger rung by default.

name: Live tier registry
description: Maps a tier name to the newest live model id by bucketing a provider's latest-first list by family, caching the result, using a last-known fallback only when the live list is empty, and exposing the next lower tier and vision capability.
advantages: Tracks new releases automatically and never fails resolution when the provider is unreachable.
disadvantages: The fallback map can go stale, and bucketing by family substring depends on provider naming conventions.

name: Subscription allowance limit detector
description: Detects a subscription usage-limit message in a run's result, parses its reset time and zone, computes a resume time, and records the limit lane-wide with optional persistence so other work waits.
advantages: Resumes after the real reset instead of retrying uselessly, and survives a restart when persistence is configured.
disadvantages: Depends on parsing human-readable wording and time zones, which can change without notice.
